Kazakhstan Imposes Temporary Ban on Crude Oil Exports, Impacting Producers

NUR-SULTAN, June 19—Kazakhstan’s government has imposed a temporary ban on crude oil exports in response to domestic fuel shortages, disrupting operations across the Oil & Gas Producers industry, including state-run KazMunayGas National Co JSC.

The embargo, announced late Tuesday by the Ministry of Energy, took immediate effect and is set to last for at least 60 days. Officials cited the need to stabilize domestic fuel supplies and prevent further price spikes at the pump. “Ensuring energy security for our citizens is our top priority,” Deputy Energy Minister Alisher Zhaksylykov said at a press briefing. “This measure is necessary under the current circumstances, but we are monitoring the situation closely.”

The embargo has halted planned shipments through key export pipelines to international markets, including Europe and China. Industry analysts estimate that the ban could affect up to 1.2 million barrels per day of crude exports, a significant portion of Kazakhstan’s output.

KazMunayGas National Co JSC confirmed in a statement that it is “assessing the operational and financial impacts” of the measure. “We are working with authorities to ensure compliance and to support efforts to stabilize the domestic market,” the company said.

The Union of Oil & Gas Producers of Kazakhstan expressed concern about potential losses. “This abrupt halt in exports could lead to storage constraints and impact revenues across the sector,” said union spokesperson Timur Kadyrov.

While the government has pledged to review the ban as the fuel situation develops, trade groups warn prolonged restrictions could strain the industry’s finances. The export embargo remains in force as of Wednesday.
